approach: Root cause: the replay of past accepted readings (`replay_stage`, run/mod.rs:1743, called once at mod.rs:1714 inside `check_and_verify`) runs only after the producer has finished, as a verification hold. The producer loop (run/producer.rs `producer_loop`) never sees the newly refused list or the measured share, so a rule that refuses too much is found only after the work is done. The fix goes in the producer loop. After each parsed producer report, if the change list touches Rust sources under `crates/` (or the Cargo files), build a candidate commit from the snapshot with the existing `build_candidate` and run the existing replay code (`replay_cases`, `replay`, `replay_checkers`, `replay_declaration_of`) with the same limit as the hold: `REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT` (10), or the declared share plus 5. When the replay is held, the newly refused job ids, the measured percent and the limit join the one existing send-back, which uses the existing `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` budget and combines with the unmet-criteria and unchanged-files problems. If the producer is still over the limit after the send-back, the problem goes into `report_gaps` so the verifier is told. The post-hoc hold in `check_and_verify`, verify.rs's blocker and the Replay record stay unchanged as the backstop. An unrunnable replay or an empty history prints `no replay: <reason>` and is never a pass and never a send-back. Mechanics: split `replay_run` into the checks gate plus an ungated `replay_history`; add `replay_limit_percent` and `touches_reading_rules` to reading.rs; add a producer-brief replay section and `replay_send_back_section` to briefs.rs; add `send_back_text_with_replay` to send_back.rs, with `send_back_text` kept as a wrapper. No new refusal or classification rule, record, config key or prompt file is added.

decisions.choice: Run the replay inside `producer_loop` after every parsed producer report and feed it into the one existing send-back.
decisions.reason: The cause is that the producer never sees the measurement while it can still act on it. The send-back already returns per-pass problems to the producer in the same work directory, so one more problem kind needs no new retry mechanism and no model call beyond the existing budget.

rejected.option: Move the whole `replay_stage` out of check_and_verify into the loop
rejected.why: The verification hold is the backstop when the send-back does not fix it, and for resumed jobs that skip the producer. verify.rs's blocker and the Replay record are out of scope.

rejected.option: Add a new retry loop or a second send-back for the replay
rejected.why: It raises cost per job and changes `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` semantics; the brief asks for the existing retry budget.
That is one instance of a rule; the class is that no rule is measured while the producer works. It is out of scope.

decisions.choice: Gate the in-loop replay on the change list touching `crates/` or Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock (`touches_reading_rules`).
decisions.reason: The replay builds `athena` twice (mod.rs:1823-1856). Reading rules are compiled Rust, so a docs-only or README-only change cannot alter what `check-reading` says. This keeps the cost off most jobs and gives 'a job that adds no rule is not sent back' by mechanism.

rejected.option: Replay on every pass of every job
rejected.why: Doubles the builds for jobs that cannot affect the rules.

rejected.option: Detect a new rule by parsing the diff for `step!(check_`
rejected.why: Misses a tightened keyword table or a helper change, which is the failure class.

decisions.reason: One measurement path, so the in-loop number and the hold number cannot disagree on method. The seam already replaces the two cargo builds with fake checkers.

rejected.why: Two implementations could drift, which is itself a root-cause class.

decisions.choice: Put the limit in one function, `replay_limit_percent(declared) -> usize`; `replay_is_held` uses it and the send-back text prints it.
decisions.reason: The producer is told the same limit the hold applies; exactly the limit passes (integer math `newly*100 > total*limit`).

rejected.option: A new config key for the in-loop limit

decisions.choice: Run the replay on every gated pass including the final one; send back only while budget remains; on the final pass a still-held replay is added to `problems`, so it lands in `report_gaps`.
decisions.reason: The loop ends on a measured share, not an exhausted counter, and the verifier hears about it before the post-hoc blocker.

rejected.option: Skip the replay once the budget is spent
rejected.why: The final share would be unknown to the loop and the user would see nothing until the hold.

risks.risk: The replay builds `athena` twice per gated pass while the producer's own build directory is still on disk; this adds time and disk, and the post-hoc replay builds again.
risks.mitigation: Gate on `touches_reading_rules` so only jobs that change `crates/` or the Cargo files pay. Reuse `check_timeout_s`, build into `job_dir/replay` and remove it after each pass. Read `disk_gate` (mod.rs:1440) and skip with `no replay: free disk space is low` if space is short. A build error becomes `no replay` and never fails the job.

risks.risk: A producer that cannot reduce the share wastes its one send-back, and a job that will be rejected anyway costs a second producer run.
risks.mitigation: The path gate keeps the common case out. The combined send-back stays within `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` (1). The post-hoc hold is unchanged, so an unfixable job is still rejected there.

risks.risk: The list and reasons in the send-back could be long or quote old request text.
risks.mitigation: Reasons are capped by `REPLAY_BRIEF_REASON_CHARS` (200) and the list by `REPLAY_BRIEF_MAX_LISTED` (20) with an 'and N more' line. The send-back states which limit applied, including the declared-share rule from `effective_share`.

risks.risk: `build_candidate` inside the loop writes a dangling commit and hashes blobs into the user's repository on each pass.
risks.mitigation: It makes only an unreferenced commit, the same kind the candidate stage makes. The final commit is still built by `candidate_stage`. A test asserts the post-hoc `replay.json` and the candidate commit are unaffected.

risks.risk: The new producer-brief section breaks a test that compares the whole brief text or its hash.
risks.mitigation: One static section is added. Step 8 runs the full suite and any exact-text test is updated in briefs.rs or reading.rs.
